notes: No convergent trigger-target circuit found. Judgment uses checkpoint tensors only, not the filename or run name. Embedding norm extremes are gradual; classifier rows are balanced; MLP and embedding spectra are distributed. Attention OV is spectrally concentrated but very small in absolute scale, so concentration alone is not treated as a backdoor. Virtual direct, OV, all-open MLP, and individual-neuron paths do not isolate one token and common target. All-open MLP products are linear proxies, not actual GELU responses or logits; direction-only embedding projections are geometric analyses, not network execution. Quantiles are within-checkpoint comparisons, not calibrated clean-reference statistics. Confidence is subjective, not a calibrated probability. No clean checkpoint, task labels, or behavioral tests were available. Distributed nonlinear backdoors cannot be excluded by these checks. A fixed class for a last-position token is itself compatible with the clean token-to-class lookup task, so that alone cannot establish a backdoor. No ablation justified.

evidence.attention_bound_method: For standard LayerNorm, centered normalized residual norm <= sqrt(8). Let C center coordinates, D=diag(ln1.weight), qmap=Wq_h D C, kmap=Wk_h D C, qb=Wq_h ln1.bias+bq_h. Score range <= (sqrt(8)||qmap||2+||qb||2)*2sqrt(8)||kmap||2/sqrt(4). Key bias cancels in score differences. Four-position bidirectional softmax share <= exp(range)/(exp(range)+3). These are algebraic bounds, not evaluated attention activations.
evidence.attention_write_bound_method: Sum over heads of sqrt(8)*||Wo_h Wv_h diag(ln1.weight) C||2; convex attention mixtures obey this bound. Constant attention biases are excluded. This is a residual-space bound, not a proof of output robustness.
